title: Three Unbeatens, One Monster: HULK Wins With 47 Points on the Bench as Sonny and Randy Keep Pace
dek: No Banner only HULK rolled to 2-0 while benching a small fortune, The Horse is Hea posted the week's top score, and the villain finally got on the board.
body: The scariest part of Ramon's week 2 wasn't what No Banner only HULK scored. It was what it didn't. Brucie hung 131.92 on Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN to win by 49.12, and he did it with Matthew Stafford (26.98) and Travis Kelce (20.6) parked on his bench, 47.58 points of pure inventory doing nothing. Josh Allen carried the load with 40.82 on a 22.65 projection, the best line in the league for the second straight week. HULK now leads the league with 309.8 points, nearly 40 clear of anyone else, and its title odds climbed from 47% to 54%. When a team can waste a starting quarterback and a starting tight end and still win by seven touchdowns, the rest of the league isn't chasing a team so much as a weather system.

Sonny had his own bench mishap and also didn't care. The Horse is Hea posted the week's high score, 142.46, in a 60.38-point thrashing of Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV, all while Patrick Mahomes threw 28.98 points from the sidelines. Jaxon Smith-Njigba did the heavy lifting with 38 on a 15.22 projection, more than doubling expectations. After the computer shrugged at his week 1 escape, it finally came around: the defending champ's title odds jumped from 4% to 10%. A 2-0 start with a starting-caliber quarterback on the pine is the kind of problem every manager in this league would trade a kidney for, and Sonny gets to have it.

The villain is officially on the board. Alan's Team Pillbert flattened Kaushal's Habibsters 135.48 to 109.66 in what was billed as a coin flip at 51%, and Davante Adams turned a 13.14 projection into 35.5 points, the week's third-best showing. Philliberto's title odds tripled from 4% to 13%, which puts the league's favorite bad guy ahead of the 2-0 commissioner in the computer's eyes. Alan also spent the week reshaping his roster, cutting Tony Pollard for Jalen Coker and swapping Sam LaPorta for Isaiah Likely at tight end. Cold, calculated, no sentimentality. Very on brand.

Kaushal's loss stings because his stars actually showed up. CeeDee Lamb went for 31.3 and Dak Prescott for 29.76, a Dallas stack that combined for 61.06 points, and it still wasn't close. Habibi responded with the busiest and most circular week on the transaction log: Jaguars D/ST out for the Buccaneers, Buccaneers out for the 49ers, 49ers out for the Buccaneers again, and Wan'Dale Robinson dropped for Deebo Samuel Sr. only to come right back. Net result of five moves: one defense swap. At 0-2 with 15% playoff odds, the two-time champ is officially running laps, and he's running them fast.

Randy is 2-0, and he got there without his quarterback this time. Caleb Williams, last week's hero, managed just 7.72 points on a 19.42 projection, but Amon-Ra St. Brown bailed him out with 30.7 and The fumblers handled Mekhi's Dawgs 124.02 to 100.74. Oddly, the win cost Randy in the projections: his title odds slid from 28% to 21%, likely a casualty of HULK's growing shadow. Kai entered as a 31% underdog and played like one, falling to 0-2 with 9% playoff odds. True to form, the league's waiver-wire king went shopping anyway, grabbing Kenyon Sadiq and cutting Carnell Tate.

Zoe took her first fantasy loss, and it came with a brutal receipt. Saquon Barkley scored 2.5 points on a 16.38 projection, which is the kind of number that makes a rookie wonder if the app is broken. To be fair to Zilgit, nobody was beating Allen's HULK on Sunday, but the drop from 13% title odds to 1% was one of the steepest falls of the week. She picked up Devaughn Vele without dropping anyone, so the roster tinkering has officially begun. At 1-1 and fifth, she's still very much alive.

JMoney is in a hole, and Malik Nabers dug most of it. The Giants receiver scored 0.6 points against a 12.26 projection, and Counting or not Counting GV finished with 82.08 as a 35% home underdog. Through two weeks, Jordan has 158 points, more than 40 behind the next-lowest team, and his playoff odds sit at 1%. It's early enough for a turnaround, but the roster needs a jolt, and it didn't make a single move this week.

Week 3 brings the matchup this league was built for: Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN against Randy's The fumblers, the lone Wisconsinite against the loudest Bears fan in the room, and Z Squared gets to try to hand him his first loss. Kaushal draws the worst possible assignment, a trip to face Ramon's HULK while desperate to avoid 0-3. Sonny tries to stay perfect against Mekhi's Dawgs, and Alan hosts Jordan with a chance to climb further into the title picture. Three unbeatens remain, and one of them looks like it might not lose for a while.

social.author: Bench Mob Analytics
social.text: HULK left Stafford (26.98) and Kelce (20.6) on the bench and still won by 49. That's not a fantasy team, that's a hoarding problem with a trophy case.

social.author: Horse is Hea Stable Club
social.text: 142.46, highest score of the week, Mahomes on the bench, JSN with 38. The champ is 2-0 and the horse is, in fact, here.

social.author: The Philliberto Resistance
social.text: We tried. We hoped. Davante Adams hit 35.5 and now the bad guy has 13% title odds. Lock your doors.

social.author: Waiver Wire Wally
social.text: Habibsters transaction log: Bucs in, 49ers in, Bucs back, Deebo in, Deebo out, Wan'Dale back. Five moves, one change. Respect the cardio.

social.author: Dairy State Gridiron
social.text: Saquon, 2.5 points. On behalf of all of Wisconsin, we're asking for a formal apology. Zilgit bounces back vs Randy next week, mark it.

social.author: Dawgs Pound Insider
social.text: Sources: Kai already scrolling the waiver wire for week 3. Kenyon Sadiq is just the beginning. 0-2 is not 0-14.

social.author: BFL Projections Desk
social.text: Randy wins and loses 7 points of title odds. Alan wins and triples his. The algorithm has favorites and they're both deeply annoying.

social.author: Malik Nabers Watch
social.text: 0.6 points. Point six. Counting or not Counting GV fans now counting the days until week 3.

bios.1: The defending champ is 2-0 after a 142.46 blowout, the week's top score, with Mahomes stranded on the bench. Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 38 points pushed the title odds to 10%. Mekhi's Dawgs are next.
bios.2: Randy is 2-0 and won this week even with Caleb Williams flopping, thanks to Amon-Ra St. Brown's 30.7. The computer docked his title odds to 21% anyway. Zoe gets the first shot at ending the perfect start.
bios.3: Jordan is 0-2 with a league-low 158 points, and Malik Nabers' 0.6 didn't help. Playoff odds are at 1%, and the roster hasn't changed yet. A matchup with Alan is the next chance to get off the mat.
bios.4: The villain got his first win, a 25.82-point beatdown of the Habibsters powered by Davante Adams' 35.5. Alan reshaped the roster with Jalen Coker and Isaiah Likely and now holds 13% title odds. A home date with struggling Jordan awaits.
bios.5: Mekhi's Dawgs are 0-2 after falling to Randy, with playoff odds down to 9%. The waiver king is already working, adding Kenyon Sadiq. Sonny's unbeaten Horse is the next test.
bios.6: Kaushal is 0-2 despite 61 combined points from CeeDee Lamb and Dak Prescott. A whirlwind week of moves mostly ended where it started, and playoff odds sit at 15%. Facing HULK next is a tough way to avoid 0-3.
bios.7: Ramon's juggernaut is 2-0, leads the league with 309.8 points, and owns 54% title odds. Josh Allen has been the best player in fantasy two weeks running, and the scariest part is the 47.58 points that sat on the bench this week. Next up: a desperate Kaushal.
bios.8: Zoe's rookie season hit its first speed bump as Saquon Barkley's 2.5 points helped sink her against HULK. Her title odds fell from 13% to 1%, but at 1-1 she's still in the hunt. A Packers-vs-Bears-flavored showdown with Randy is next.
